videos.title: Why are AI data centers using so much electricity?
videos.focus: Independent educational analysis of AI data-center electricity, water, cooling and infrastructure tradeoffs
videos.summary: TED-Ed explains why training and serving large AI models requires dense clusters of accelerators, networking, electricity and cooling. complete_compiler_story.headline: LifeVal tests AI help on everyday planning decisions

audience_fit.intended_user: People comparing AI assistance for household planning, budgeting, childcare, government services and other ordinary decisions.
audience_fit.practical_action: Choose one low-stakes planning task, state constraints and sources, compare the assistant’s recommendation with the underlying information and record what remains uncertain.
audience_fit.review_action: The user verifies dates, costs, eligibility rules and consequential assumptions with the original provider before acting.
audience_fit.usable_outcome: A reviewed planning note that separates the assistant’s proposal, verified facts, unresolved questions and the person’s final decision.

source.title: Introducing LifeVal
source.scope: Read the complete OpenAI LifeVal article covering its 3,995-respondent survey, everyday task construction, childcare, government-service and budgeting examples, evaluation approach, benchmark-over-time design and limitations of self-reported priorities and model-produced assistance.
source.freshness_reason: The publisher exposes a November 2 date without a publication time, so rolling-24-hour freshness is unproven. complete_compiler_story.headline: A decision-review Skill keeps AI initiatives tied to evidence
complete_compiler_story.agent_skills_evidence: The first-party Databricks article defines five decision disciplines and four operating foundations for enterprise AI initiatives. This edition turns them into a reusable noncoding procedure: write the business problem, evidence, accountable owner, full cost and stop-or-expand criteria; review assumptions; then record a decision and next observation. The source, action and outcome are distinct from prior recommendation-audit and release-control Skills.

audience_fit.intended_user: Business owners, operations leaders and review groups deciding whether to start, continue, change or stop an AI initiative.
audience_fit.practical_action: Complete a one-page review with the business problem, evidence, accountable owner, full cost, key assumptions and explicit stop-or-expand criteria.
audience_fit.review_action: A named reviewer challenges unsupported claims, checks source evidence and confirms that the decision and next measurement follow the stated criteria.
audience_fit.usable_outcome: A reusable decision-review record with cited evidence, accountable ownership, bounded cost, assumptions, a documented decision and a dated next observation.

source.scope: Read the complete Databricks essay covering five decision disciplines, four operating foundations, business-problem definition, evidence, ownership, full costs, flexibility, learning loops and the limits of vendor-authored management guidance.

complete_compiler_story.related_coverage: Turns broad AI-strategy advice into a repeatable evidence review that produces a documented continue, change or stop decision.
complete_compiler_story.summary: Databricks proposes five disciplines for enterprise AI decisions: define the business problem, use evidence, assign ownership, count full costs and preserve flexibility. The article is management guidance, not outcome proof. A reusable Skill converts those prompts into a one-page review with cited assumptions, explicit stop-or-expand criteria, a recorded decision and a dated next observation.
complete_compiler_story.why_it_matters: Teams can use the Skill before buying or scaling anything: challenge the evidence, name the accountable owner, include integration and review costs and decide what result would stop the initiative. That makes learning inspectable and reversible.
